bib.title: Are Emergent Abilities of Large Language Models a Mirage?

question: Are the sharp, unpredictable emergent abilities of LLMs a property of scale or an artefact of the metric chosen by the researcher?
hypothesis: Emergent abilities appear because of nonlinear or discontinuous metrics (and too little test data to resolve small models), not because of fundamental changes in model behaviour with scale.
contributions: A simple mathematical model of how nonlinear/discontinuous metrics turn smooth per-token error into apparent emergence
Three predictions tested on the InstructGPT/GPT-3 family
Two predictions tested in a meta-analysis of BIG-Bench claims
Metric-induced emergent abilities in vision tasks across diverse architectures

method.summary: Analytic model: per-token cross-entropy falls as a power law, so accuracy over L tokens is exp(-(N/c)^alpha)^L, sharp on a linear-log plot, while token edit distance is near-linear. Tested by rescoring fixed GPT-3 family outputs on 2-shot arithmetic, by meta-analysing published BIG-Bench results (incl. LaMDA Brier score), and by training small vision models and redefining accuracy as all-K-correct.
method.task: Metric analysis of claimed emergent abilities (arithmetic with GPT-3 family, BIG-Bench meta-analysis, vision classification/reconstruction)

datasets.name: InstructGPT/GPT-3 arithmetic outputs
datasets.source: collected via OpenAI API; 2-shot 2-integer 2-digit multiplication and 2-shot 2-integer 4-digit addition
datasets.preprocessing: Fig 4 uses additional generated test data to raise resolution; number of test items not stated

datasets.name: BIG-Bench published results
datasets.size: 39 preferred metrics; >=220 tasks, ~40 metrics per task, ~10 model families (~10^6 triplets, Discussion)
datasets.source: Srivastava et al. 2022; hand annotations of emergence by Wei 2022 ('137 emergent abilities')
datasets.preprocessing: emergence score (Eq. 1) computed per task-metric-model family

datasets.name: Omniglot
datasets.preprocessing: images embedded by convolutional layers; sequences of image-label pairs, length L in [1,5]

other.availability: 4 models available via OpenAI API as of 2023-03-15

other.note: outputs taken from BIG-Bench; no sizes stated

models.name: Shallow nonlinear autoencoder family
models.architecture: single hidden layer nonlinear autoencoder, varying bottleneck units

models.name: Autoregressive causal Transformer family (Omniglot)
models.architecture: decoder-only transformer with conv image embedding

training.objective: inferred: reconstruction MSE (autoencoder) and classification (LeNet, Omniglot transformer); not stated

other.note: only the vision models are trained; no training hyperparameters are given in the paper

parameters.mnist_K: 1 to 5 (text); Fig 10 legend shows 6, 8, 10 for some curves

metrics.name: Accuracy (exact string match)
metrics.definition: 1 if no additions, no deletions and all L tokens match the target, else 0

metrics.name: Token edit distance
metrics.definition: Num substitutions + additions + deletions to turn target into output; plotted negated

metrics.name: Multiple choice grade
metrics.definition: 1 if highest probability mass on correct option, else 0

metrics.name: Brier score
metrics.definition: for a binary outcome, mean squared error between outcome and predicted probability mass

metrics.name: Emergence score
metrics.definition: sign(argmax y - argmin y)(max y - min y)/sqrt(Median((y_i-y_{i-1})^2)), from Srivastava et al.

metrics.name: Reconstruction_c
metrics.definition: mean over test data of indicator that squared reconstruction error < c

eval.protocol: Fixed model outputs rescored under different metrics; no seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests reported.

evidence.quote: As of 2023-03-15, 4 models with 350M, 1.3B, 6.7B, 175B parameters are available via the OpenAI API.

results.claim: Over 92% of claimed BIG-Bench emergent abilities (Wei hand annotations) appear under just two metrics, Multiple Choice Grade and Exact String Match.
results.setup: Hand-annotated task-metric-model family triplets from Wei 2022 on BIG-Bench; 4 of 39 preferred metrics show any annotated emergence
results.quote: 2 metrics account for > 92% of claimed emergent abilities (Fig. 5C): Multiple Choice Grade and Exact String Match.

results.claim: Under the automatic emergence score, at most 5 of 39 preferred BIG-Bench metrics show emergence for any task-model family pair.
results.setup: Emergence score (Eq. 1) over all BIG-Bench tasks
results.quote: of the 39 preferred metrics in BIG-Bench, at most 5 display emergence (Fig. 5A)
results.note: Hand annotation gives 4/39 metrics instead (Fig 5B). The >92% figure belongs to the hand-annotated set, not to the emergence-score set.

results.claim: Hand-annotated emergence appears under only 4 of 39 metrics.
results.quote: revealed emergent abilities appear with 4/39 metrics (Fig. 5B)

results.claim: On InstructGPT/GPT-3 arithmetic, switching from Accuracy to Token Edit Distance on the same fixed outputs turns sharp emergence into smooth improvement with scale.
results.setup: 2-shot 2-digit x 2-digit multiplication and 4-digit + 4-digit addition; 350M to 175B; target length 1 to 5; temperature 0 and 1
results.quote: if one changes from nonlinear Accuracy to linear Token Edit Distance while keeping the models' outputs fixed, the family's performance smoothly, continuously
results.note: Qualitative, read from figure; no numeric scores given.

results.claim: With more test data, even the smallest GPT-3 models score above chance on Accuracy and accuracy falls roughly geometrically with target length.
results.setup: Same arithmetic tasks, extra generated test data (count not stated)
results.quote: all models in the InstructGPT/GPT-3 family achieve above-chance accuracy (Fig. 4)

results.claim: LaMDA emergent abilities seen under Multiple Choice Grade vanish under Brier Score on the same tasks.
results.setup: LaMDA outputs from BIG-Bench; tasks chosen because LaMDA shows emergence under Multiple Choice Grade; number of tasks not stated
results.quote: LaMDA's emergent abilities on the discontinuous Multiple Choice Grade disappeared when we changed the metric to the continuous Brier Score (Fig. 6).

results.claim: Metric choice induces apparent emergence in vision models: shallow autoencoders (CIFAR100, Reconstruction_c), Omniglot causal transformers and LeNet on MNIST (all-K-correct accuracy).
results.setup: Smoothly improving base metric (MSE, per-item accuracy) redefined as thresholded or all-correct
results.quote: the autoencoder family exhibits a sharp and seemingly unpredictable image reconstruction ability (Fig. 7C)

results.claim: The paper estimates about 10^6 task-metric-model family triplets in BIG-Bench, so some apparent emergence by chance is likely.
results.setup: BIG-Bench: >=220 tasks, ~40 metrics per task, ~10 model families; an order-of-magnitude estimate, no test run
results.quote: for a total of ∼106 task-metric-model family triplets
results.note: Text extraction renders 10^6 as '106'. No multiple-comparison correction was actually computed.

results.claim: Authors state they do not claim LLMs cannot show emergent abilities.
results.quote: nothing in this paper should be interpreted as claiming that large language models cannot display emergent abilities

limits: Authors concede the independence-of-tokens approximation is false and per-token error is assumed constant (Sec 2 fn 1; App A).
Only the GPT-3 family (4 sizes) is analysed from raw outputs; other families (PaLM, LaMDA etc.) only via published numbers.
Paper says it does not show LLMs cannot have emergent abilities; it says previously claimed ones 'might likely be a mirage'.
Number of test items, tasks for LaMDA, and all vision training hyperparameters are not stated; no seeds, intervals or significance tests.
Vision demonstrations show metrics can create emergence, not that LLM emergence is only metric-induced.
Arithmetic and the 350M to 175B range are narrow; later work and models after 2023 not covered.

terms.definition: abilities that are not present in smaller-scale models but are present in large-scale models; thus they cannot be predicted by simply extrapolating the performance improvements on smaller-scale models (quoting Wei et al.)
The smallest interval measurable by a scientific instrument; the resolving power. Here set by 1/test dataset size (1/NL for per-token error).

figures.caption: Emergent abilities of large language models are created by the researcher's chosen metrics, not unpredictable changes in model behavior with scale.
figures.why: Six panels show one smooth loss curve yielding sharp or smooth curves depending on metric

figures.caption: Claimed emergent abilities evaporate upon changing the metric.
figures.why: Same GPT-3 outputs under Accuracy (sharp) and Token Edit Distance (smooth)

figures.caption: Emergent abilities appear only for specific metrics, not task-model families.
figures.why: Counts of metrics showing emergence in BIG-Bench

code.snippet: Accuracy(N) ≈ p_N(single token correct)^(num. of tokens) = exp(-(N/c)^alpha)^L ; Token Edit Distance(N) ≈ L(1 - exp(-(N/c)^alpha))
